title: A Harvest for the Visitor
premise: Cyrus Yarrow, a hospice nurse who has spent a decade rationalizing the backwards counting they hear from the dying, is pulled into a nightmare when an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the town's old well. The door belongs to the Visitor, an entity that harvests the town once a generation, sustained by a harvest song whose final verse has been deliberately forgotten by the founding families. As neighbors vanish and the well begins to refill, Cyrus must recover the last verse from the town's oldest dying resident — while refusing to sing along, because singing it is what feeds the Visitor. In the end, Cyrus sings the verse alone, backwards, sealing the door from the outside at the cost of their own voice and their place in the town that finally, too late, claimed them as one of its own.
about_author: Jonah Quintana is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent six years listening to the last words of strangers and swears half of them were counting. A Harvest for the Visitor is their second novel, written entirely between the hours of 2 and 4 a.m.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: Cyrus Yarrow's POV. On the hospice night shift, a dying woman counts backwards from thirty and stops at nine, whispering 'the well is nearly full.' Cyrus logs it as terminal lucidity, but their hands shake. Establishes Cyrus's decade-long habit of rationalizing the noises, and the loneliness of being the only one who hears them. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: Cyrus attends the ceremony for the town's new reservoir project and meets excavation foreman Dara Okafor, who jokes that the ground 'hums when you put your ear to it.' The town's founding families — the Vessels — watch from a distance, unsmiling. Cyrus feels watched. Emotional beat: the first crack in Cyrus's rationalizations, and a sense of the town keeping a secret in plain sight.

chapters.title: What the Backhoe Found
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The crew unearths a stone door beneath the old well shaft — sealed from the inside, hinges fused, carved with verses of a song no one recognizes. One worker, Petey, hums a fragment and that night sleepwalks to the shaft. Dara calls Cyrus, the town's only nurse, when Petey is found counting backwards in his sleep. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: House Call
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus examines Petey, whose vitals are wrong in a way medicine has no word for — his heart beats in reverse rhythm, like something being drawn back in. Petey begs Cyrus to 'not learn the rest of it.' The Vessels arrive at the site and order the door covered with concrete by morning. Emotional beat: Cyrus's denial begins to fail; the horror is medical, intimate, close.

chapters.title: The Vessel Family Album
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Researching the town's history at the library, Cyrus finds the founding families' records: every generation, a 'harvest year,' a list of names that simply end. A librarian, Miss Aldous, quietly slips Cyrus a photograph of the well in 1931 — and a face in the crowd that is identical to a man still living today. Emotional beat: the thrill of forbidden knowledge, and the first proof Cyrus isn't imagining it.

chapters.title: Nine Days Short
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Petey dies at exactly the number he counted down to. At the funeral, half the town sings a lullaby under their breath that Dara realizes is the song carved on the door — but they all stop before the final verse, in unison, like a held breath. Dara confronts the pastor, who says only: 'We don't finish it. That's the whole covenant.' Emotional beat: grief and the vertigo of realizing everyone knows but Cyrus.

chapters.title: The Refill
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The dry well shaft begins to fill with black water that rises a foot each night, though no aquifer feeds it. Cyrus's hospice patients all begin counting backwards, synchronized, every night at 3:11. One of them, old Tomasin Vessel, is lucid for the first time in years and tells Cyrus: 'The door was sealed from the inside so it could only be opened by someone who wanted to come out.' Emotional beat: the countdown begins; time becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The town, for the first time, embraces Cyrus — dinners, invitations, warmth. Cyrus, ten years an outsider, is seduced by it, even as they notice the invitations always come with questions: What did Tomasin tell you? What did you hear? Dara warns Cyrus the friendliness is a test. Emotional beat: the theme of belonging weaponized; Cyrus wants to be kept even knowing they're being measured.

chapters.title: Loyalty of the Living
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The Vessels offer Dara a bribe: finish the reservoir contract, take the money, leave town before harvest. Dara refuses to abandon Cyrus or Petey's memory. That night Dara finds the crew's site trailer ransacked and the door's rubbing of the carvings stolen — the Vessels are destroying the verses one copy at a time. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen at real cost; the enemy stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Tomasin's Verse
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Tomasin, dying faster now, agrees to teach Cyrus the final verse — the verse the founding families cut from the song to starve the Visitor and trap it half-fed. He sings it once, and the hospice ward's windows frost from the inside. He warns: 'The verse only works if you mean the sacrifice. Sing it to survive and it harvests you instead.' Emotional beat: revelation and terror entwined; knowledge is a debt.

chapters.title: The Night the Counting Stopped
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Every patient in the ward falls silent at 3:11 — the counting has stopped because the well is full. The black water now stands level with the door. Cyrus finds Tomasin gone from his bed, his window open from the inside, footprints leading toward the well that end at the shaft's edge. Emotional beat: the harvest has begun, and Cyrus's one teacher is its first fruit.

chapters.title: Missing
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. People begin disappearing — not the outsiders first, but the Vessels, the covenant-keepers, taken in their sleep with their doors still locked. The town's unity fractures; some want to open the door and beg, others want to flee. The pastor hangs himself with the hymnal open to the harvest song. Emotional beat: panic; the covenant's protectors are its first payment.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Kept
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus admits the truth they've hidden for ten years: they weren't born hearing the counting — they heard it first as a child, the night their own family vanished in a harvest year, and they've been counting the years since. The town didn't adopt Cyrus; the Visitor marked them. Emotional beat: devastating self-reckoning; Cyrus's belonging was always a claim, not a gift.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Well
chapters.summary: Dara and Cyrus, alternating POV. At the shaft's edge they hear the missing singing the harvest song from beneath the water, in harmony, in reverse — and among the voices, Tomasin's, and Cyrus's mother's. The song is nearly complete; the missing are being made to sing the final verse for it. Cyrus realizes they have until the choir reaches the last line. Emotional beat: horror at maximum intimacy; the dead are the instrument.

chapters.title: The Vessels' Bargain
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The last surviving Vessel, Maren, offers Cyrus the family's secret: the door can be sealed from the outside, but only by someone the Visitor has already marked, singing the final verse backwards — a song that unravels the singer's voice, memory, and name. Maren's ancestors were too afraid to be the one. 'We kept the covenant by never finishing the sacrifice.' Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit and unbearable.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The well overflows; black water moves through the town's pipes, taps run singing. Dara evacuates who they can, but the roads loop back to the town no matter which way they drive. Dara chooses to stay with Cyrus rather than escape alone, burning the evacuation bus's fuel to keep the hospice generators running for the dying. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved on Dara's side — truth wins, at cost.

chapters.title: The Last Verse, Learned
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the hospice ward, the dying — the only ones the Visitor cannot yet take — teach Cyrus the verse backwards, line by line, each patient giving one line and dying peacefully as they give it. Cyrus memorizes what will unmake them and says goodbye to Dara without saying it. Emotional beat: elegiac; the horror's climax is prepared as an act of care.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus walks into the well shaft as the water parts, down to the door sealed from the inside, where the Visitor waits wearing the faces of everyone the town has ever harvested. It offers Cyrus everything they've wanted for ten years: an explanation, a family, a place. All Cyrus has to do is sing the verse forward, with everyone else. Emotional beat: temptation at its most compassionate; the monster's true face is belonging.

chapters.title: Sung Backwards
chapters.summary: Climax, Cyrus's POV. As the choir beneath the water reaches the final line, Cyrus sings the last verse backwards, alone, meaning the sacrifice. The song unravels; the door's hinges fuse outward; the harvested are released as light through the water. The Visitor takes Cyrus's voice, then their name, then their memories of the town — but not before Cyrus writes one word on Dara's palm. Emotional beat: triumph and annihilation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Well Runs Dry
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The water drains, the door is stone and dead, the missing are found as ash arranged in the shapes of their names. The town, freed, begins the process of forgetting — and of forgetting Cyrus. Dara alone remembers, carrying the word written on their palm: 'stay.' Dara buries the door under concrete, this time on purpose. Emotional beat: hollow victory; survival's price is memory itself.

chapters.title: The New Nurse
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV — or what remains. Months later, a quiet person works the hospice night shift, excellent at the job, unable to speak, who sometimes tilts their head at the dying as if listening. Dara visits every week and reads to them from a notebook: who they were, what they did, the word on a palm. The person always cries at the same page. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into devotion; identity survives in being remembered.

chapters.title: A Harvest for the Visitor
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Dara's POV. On the anniversary, Dara takes the mute nurse to the capped well and, for the first time in a year, the ground is silent. But at 3:11, far off in another county, a hospice patient begins counting backwards from nine. Dara holds the nurse's hand, and the nurse — who cannot speak — taps the answer against Dara's skin, one tap at a time, in the old rhythm. Emotional beat: quiet, earned dread; the price of survival is a watch that never ends.
